text: 57-year-old male. The patient reports a large wound on his right lower leg that has been present for 6 months. He mentions that his legs have been chronically swollen for over 10 years and that his mother and brother had similar leg problems. He had a documented deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in the affected leg 5 years ago but has no other significant past medical history.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Large wound on the right lower leg. I also have Chronic leg swelling, Family history of similar leg problems. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pyelonephritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That previous diagnosis of pyelonephritis (a kidney infection) does not match a leg wound; kidney infections typically present with fever, flank pain, and urinary symptoms rather than a chronic ulcer on the leg. Given your family history of similar issues and chronic swelling, could you tell me if you have ever been diagnosed with diabetes or high blood sugar?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Venous Stasis Ulcer

Based on your history of deep vein thrombosis, chronic leg swelling, and the location of your wound, this presentation is classic for a venous stasis ulcer. While we still lack specific glucose data and wound images, the clinical picture strongly points to venous insufficiency rather than arterial disease or infection.
